_about: Hand-written by the lean thread on 2026-10-31: how each checkable candidate in open-problems/candidates.json is read into the checker schema (lean/eliminate/README.md). Nothing numeric is invented: a commitment is translated only where the candidate states it; otherwise the entry is untranslatable, or a per-constraint cannot-rule reason is given. lean/eliminate/translate.mjs joins these with the original records to produce open-problems/candidates.formal.json. Reason codes: not-formalised (the claim rests on a quantity no theorem covers, chiefly strength or area scaling as L^2), premise-rejected (the candidate denies the model's own premise, so a theorem conditional on it cannot rule), outside-model (the candidate adds a term the model lacks), adopts-theorem (the candidate uses the theorem as its premise and commits no number), no-graph (C6 needs an emitted part_of graph), untranslatable.
NOT_FORMALISED: not formalised: strength, cross-section or exchange-area scaling as L^2 is not formalised; the cube law covers only the mass side (volume at constant density)
NO_GRAPH: no graph: C6 rules on an emitted part_of graph with pinned taxon statements (organism-design format); the candidate's part-of or homology claims are stated in words and were not emitted as a graph

WP-002/C1.reading: The candidate sets the growth ratio to 1 by denying the model's premise (isogamy, no males); the twofold-cost theorem is conditional on anisogamy with males contributing nothing, so it cannot rule on a model without males.

cannotRule.C5: premise-rejected: the candidate posits isogamy with no males; the theorem assumes a 1:1 sex ratio with males contributing nothing

WP-002/C2.reading: The candidate concedes anisogamy but adds a per-offspring fitness advantage (1+s >= 2) for sexual offspring; the model has equal fitness and no selection term, so the theorem cannot say whether the advantage compensates.

cannotRule.C5: outside-model: a fitness advantage of sexual offspring is not in the model (equal fecundity and viability); the theorem fixes only the twofold term the advantage must offset

WP-003/C1.reading: Parasite-induced fitness reduction of asexuals is a term the model lacks; the candidate's factor 1/2 is chosen to offset the twofold term, which the theorem fixes but cannot weigh against a reduction it does not model.

cannotRule.C5: outside-model: parasite-induced fitness reduction is not in the model; the theorem fixes only the twofold term it must offset

WP-003/C2.reading: The conceded within-population advantage 2 is read as the per-generation factor on the odds of asexual females, which is the theorem's own quantity; the lineage extinction-rate inequality is outside every constraint.
notFormalised: lineage extinction rates e_a, e_s and origination rate tau: no constraint

WP-003/C3.reading: The candidate denies equal fecundity (asexual fecundity at most 0.5 of sexual), which is the model's premise; the theorem does not say what happens under unequal fecundity.

cannotRule.C5: premise-rejected: the candidate posits unequal fecundity; the theorem assumes equal fecundity

ORX-19/C1.reading: 'Growing twice as fast at equal fecundity' is read as the odds factor 2 per generation; the lineage-lifetime ratio <= 0.1 is outside every constraint.
notFormalised: mean lineage lifetime ratio asexual:sexual: no constraint

WP-012/C2.reading: 'Demand ~ r^3' is volume (weight at constant density) with exponent 3 (C7b); 'transport capacity ~ r^2' is an area with exponent 2 (C2a, now formalised as R2); both are the hypotheses restated, so consistent; the formula r* = 3J/q is a design rule no theorem covers.
notFormalised: critical radius r* = 3J/q: a design rule beyond the scaling laws

WP-025/C1.reading: 'Weight ~ L^3' (C7b), 'supporting section ~ L^2' (C2a) and 'stress ~ L' (C8e, R7 with R1) are the theorems' own exponents under isometry; consistent. L_final = σ*/(c ρ g) is the size limit cannot_carry gives in form, with constants no theorem supplies.
notFormalised: L_final = σ*/(c ρ g): the constants c, ρ, g, σ* are not supplied by any theorem

SCI100-14/C1.reading: 'Heart mass ~ k^3' (C7b) and 'aortic cross-section ~ k^2' (C2a) are the isometry hypotheses restated; 'cross-section per unit mass ~ 1/k' follows from them and is consistent.

SCI100-17/C1.reading: 'Supported mass ~ k^3' (C7b), 'bone cross-section ~ k^2' (C2a) and 'peak bone stress ~ k' (C8e) are exactly R1, R2 and R7: consistent.

SCI100-48/C1.reading: k = 1000, mass x 1e9 (C7: 1000^3), stem cross-section x 1e6 (C2b: 1000^2) and basal stress x 1000 (C8d: 1000^1) are all consistent with R1, R2 and R7; 'height is capped by stem strength' is the existence of L_max (cannot_carry), whose value needs σ and the shape constants, not supplied.
notFormalised: the value of the height cap needs σ and the shape constant; only its existence is a theorem

SCI100-53/C1.reading: 10 t to 100 t is weight ratio 10; '2.154' is 10^(1/3) rounded (interval [2.1535, 2.1545]; a point reading would spuriously eliminate a rounding); 'bone cross-section x 4.64' is 2.154^2 rounded, read as the area exponent 2 (C2a), and 'bone stress x 2.154' as the stress exponent 1 (C8e); all consistent with R1, R2, R7. 'Unless limb bones became relatively thicker' is the allometric escape the scope note names.

ORX-17/C2.reading: 'Demand ~ L^3' (C7b) and 'exchange area ~ L^2' (C2a) are the isometry hypotheses restated; 'capacity/demand ~ 1/L' follows; consistent. That only lineages breaking isometry reach giant sizes is the contrapositive the theorems allow but do not assert.

ORX-18/C2.reading: k = 10: mass x 1000 (C7), leg cross-section and orifice area x 100 (C2b), leg stress x 10 (C8d): all consistent with R1, R2, R7; the tracheal diffusion path ~ k is a length, which no constraint covers.
notFormalised: tracheal diffusion path length ~ k: no constraint

ORX-18/C3.untranslatable: the committed figures (11% induced-power reduction, 1.19x and 1.22x maximal length, muscle mass-specific power exponent 0.24) are aerodynamic and muscle-power quantities from the source; none is a weight-versus-length commitment under isometry, so no constraint maps to them

WP-077/C1.reading: 'Blade mass ~ k^3 (thickness scales too)' is the body-like load of R9a (C7b, exponent 3); 'petiole cross-section ~ k^2' is C2a; 'petiole bending stress ~ (mass x lever arm)/section modulus ~ k^4/k^3 = k' is exactly R9a conclusion 1 (C12, exponent 1), so the candidate is consistent, not eliminated; 'the upper limit is where this stress reaches petiole strength' is the existence of L_max,b (bending_cannot_carry), whose value needs sigma_max and the shape constants. The candidate chose the R9a fork by committing to thickness scaling; under R9b (constant thickness) no limit would follow.

cannotRule.C8e: not the quantity of the lemma: C8e is axial stress W/A; the stress of this candidate is bending stress, ruled on by C12

notFormalised: the value of the petiole size limit (sigma_max and the shape constants are not supplied); wind loading (dynamic) is outside R9

ORX-14/C2.reading: 'B ~ M^(2/3)' is read as metabolic rate proportional to an exchange surface that scales as L^2 under isometry (M^(2/3) = L^2 by R1): the area exponent 2 (C2a), consistent; whether metabolism is in fact surface-limited is not a question any theorem decides.
notFormalised: that metabolic rate is limited by an exchange surface: no theorem

ORX-15/C2.reading: 'Acceleration reaction ~ L^3' (C7b, mass), 'drag ~ L^2, attachment strength ~ L^2' (C2a) and 'acceleration stress ~ L' (C8e, force ∝ L^3 over area ∝ L^2) are consistent with R1, R2, R7; 'drag stress ~ L^0' (two areas cancelling) and the limit L_max ∝ strength/(ρ du/dt) are beyond the lemmas.
notFormalised: drag stress independent of size and the value of L_max: beyond the scaling lemmas

ORX-10/C2.reading: 'Mass ~ L^3' (C7b), 'wing area ~ L^2' (C2a), 'wing loading ~ L = M^(1/3)' (C8e: W/S is the lemma's W/A) and 'minimum speed ~ M^(1/6) = L^(1/2)' (C9c, R4) are all the theorems' own exponents: consistent. 'Excess-power margin shrinks with size' rests on the muscle premise (R6), carried only as a hypothesis.
notFormalised: that muscle mass-specific power is constant (R6): a named hypothesis, not a theorem

SMC-06/C2.reading: 'Demand ~ r^3' (C7b) and 'supply ~ r^2' (C2a) are the hypotheses restated: consistent; r_max = 3J/q is a design rule no theorem covers.
notFormalised: r_max = 3J/q: a design rule beyond the scaling laws

WP-055/C1.reading: 'Under neutrality the divergence within the window is 2 mu T_w' commits each lineage's substitution rate to equal mu = 1e-9 per site per year (the identity k = mu is unit-free, so per-year values are checked as given); the window T_w = 20 Myr is not checked by any constraint (no M, no site count).

WP-055/C2.reading: As WP-055/C1: the excess divergence 2 mu x 100 Myr commits k = mu = 1e-9 per site per year; the 100 Myr lead time is not checked by any constraint.

WP-056/C1.untranslatable: adopts-theorem: mu is given no value; the candidate states the neutral budget mu x Delta per site, which is the theorem's own expression, and commits to no quantity a constraint could contradict

SCI25-11/C1.reading: '2 mu T = 0.6% for mu = 1e-8, T = 3e5' commits k = mu = 1e-8 per site per generation (C1) and T = 3e5 generations; the count of selected changes (< 100) is outside every constraint; the supply ceiling C3b needs M and the site count, which are not given.
notFormalised: fewer than 100 positively selected regulatory changes: no constraint

SCI100-11/C1.untranslatable: adopts-theorem: the insertion mutation rate is given no value; '330 bp per genome per year' is a requirement derived from the two genome sizes, not a commitment of k against mu; the candidate uses k = mu as its premise

ORX-20/C1.untranslatable: adopts-theorem: the candidate uses k = mu (reading third-position substitution rates as mutation rates, which the theorem licenses under neutrality) and reports 100-fold variation in mutation rate across species; no (k, mu) pair for one lineage is committed and nothing contradicts k = mu

ORX-20/C2.reading: 'Caused by differences in effective population size' is read as two lineages with the same mutation rate (ratio 1) whose synonymous substitution rates differ 100-fold (the source's figure), synonymous sites being neutral as the candidate's framing presupposes; if the candidate instead meant that synonymous sites are under selection, the constraint does not apply, and the row would be cannot-rule.

SCI100-44/C1.untranslatable: adopts-theorem: 'fixation rate = transfer rate' and 'fixation probability i/M' are the theorem's own statements applied to transfer events; no M, no rate and no probability is given a value

SCI100-44/C2.untranslatable: adopts-theorem: 'fixation probability at least i/M for s > 0' is the favored-floor theorem itself; no M, s or probability is given a value

ORX-05/C1.untranslatable: adopts-theorem: 'reversal rate = reversal mutation rate' and 'fixation probability 1/M' are the theorem's own statements; no M or rate is given a value

ORX-07/C2.untranslatable: adopts-theorem: u and G are given no values; the candidate states the neutral expectation u G (the theorem) and a dichotomy (u < 1/G or non-neutrality) that no constraint decides

WP-034/C2.untranslatable: adopts-theorem: 'fixation probability equals current frequency' is the i/M theorem; no M, frequency or probability is given a value

WP-032/C1.untranslatable: adopts-theorem: 'fixes with probability equal to its frequency and is substituted at its mutation rate' restates both theorems; no value is committed

WP-075/C2.reading: 'Additive genetic variance in fitness from intragenotypic differences is 0 by definition' and 'selection on that variance raises mean fitness each generation' are read as variance 0 with a positive change in mean fitness under one round of selection at one haploid locus (C4c).

EVO-02/C1.untranslatable: adopts-theorem: 'between-species substitution rate per locus equals the locus mutation rate for neutral loci' is the theorem; no locus rate is given a value; the covariation pattern is a prediction no constraint decides

EVO-10/C2.reading: 'Stasis because V_A(fitness) = 0' is read as variance 0 with zero change in mean fitness; the theorem agrees (consistent) and does not test whether the variance is in fact zero.

EVO-12/C1.untranslatable: the candidate commits to no twofold-cost quantity; the asexual growth advantage is background to an extinction-rate claim that no constraint decides

cannotRule.C6: no-graph: the digit position-to-identity map is stated in words, not emitted as a part_of graph with taxon statements

ORX-04/C1.reading: A homology map across taxa could be checked by C6 only as an emitted graph; none was emitted.

cannotRule.C6: no-graph: the single-shift claim across a theropod tree is stated in words, not emitted as a part_of graph

ORX-04/C2.reading: As ORX-04/C1; the number of shift events is not a quantity any constraint covers.

cannotRule.C6: no-graph: the six-segment, one-to-one homology map is stated in words, not emitted as a part_of graph with taxon statements

WP-088/C1.reading: The segment count 6 is not a quantity any constraint covers; the homology map could be checked by C6 only as an emitted graph.

cannotRule.C6: no-graph: the ocular-segment root claim is stated in words, not emitted as a part_of graph

WP-088/C2.reading: A change of the hierarchy's root could be checked by C6 (rootedness) only on an emitted graph; none was emitted.

cannotRule.C6: no-graph: the carapace part-of exite part-of leg-segment homology is stated in words, not emitted as a part_of graph with taxon statements

ORX-06/C1.reading: The candidate commits to no quantity; its part-of chain could be checked for acyclicity and taxon consistency by C6 only as an emitted graph.

cannotRule.C6: no-graph: the root organism P with parts {S, R} is stated in words, not emitted as a part_of graph

SMC-05/C1.reading: The group size 32, propagule size 1 and 5 divisions are not quantities any constraint covers; the part-of structure P > {S, R} could be checked by C6 only as an emitted graph.
notFormalised: group size at fragmentation, propagule size, divisions per cycle: no constraint

cannotRule.C6: no-graph: the organ O with exactly one host-tissue parent and no part containing O is itself a well-formedness condition, but it is stated in words, not emitted as a part_of graph with taxon statements

SMC-06/C1.reading: The candidate's commitment (exactly one parent; no part contains O; parts are cell types of the host taxon or declared synthetic) is precisely what C6 checks, on an emitted graph; none was emitted.
